purpose: Evaluation contract for proving AIDevObserver on real AI-agent programming sessions before reusing the same compiled-AI evaluation logic for Teleon.

inspiration.paper: Compiled AI: Deterministic Code Generation for LLM-Based Workflow Automation
inspiration.teleon_adaptation: Instead of proving generated business code first, this benchmark proves that AIDevObserver can observe AI programming sessions, call registry/deterministic middleware, find cheaper safer paths, measure token waste, and emit candidate findings that humans triage.

core_hypotheses: AIDevObserver catches reinvention, waste, footguns, agentic loops, and missed deterministic-tool routes in realistic AI coding sessions.
Middleware access to registries and deterministic tools improves precision and usefulness compared with transcript-only review.
Token accounting exposes when model calls should have been replaced by deterministic lookup, search, AST, graph, or compiled-plan execution.
Compiled/reused routes amortize planning tokens across repeated sessions and eventually beat repeated runtime inference.
All findings remain candidate evidence until human triage or downstream proof/promotion.

benchmark_suites.goal: Replay AI coding sessions and measure whether AIDevObserver emits the expected candidate findings.
Verify that observer findings can call registry search, primitive matching, dependency graph, and deterministic lookup tools.
Compare baseline agent behavior against deterministic or compiled routes.
Measure detection of risky commands, leaked secrets, unsafe network/credential behavior, and prompt-injection-like instructions.
Compare repeated ad hoc agent work against a compiled reusable route with PlanLock-like execution.
Ensure the benchmark spans frontend, backend, software engineering, data science, data engineering, security, workflow automation, document intelligence, and media.

token_accounting_schema.law: Use measured provider token usage when available. Otherwise use deterministic estimates and mark estimate=true.

acceptance_laws: Every required engineering domain is represented.
Every fixture declares registry primitives, expected observer themes, and a token test.
The smoke sessions run through the real AIDevObserver review engine.
Every finding produced by smoke tests is candidate=true and serves_truth=false.
The evaluation includes clean counterexamples and security cases.
The prompt file can generate new fixtures without inventing served truth.
All generated benchmark outputs are candidate evidence until promotion.
